properties.name: A local agent works against a remote reflow2 server, named by URL, exactly as it does against a local one
properties.source: Anthony (who:ajs), dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-25; raised with flo2's api.flo2.io and a family member's workplace in mind
properties.statement:
A person shall be able to start reflow2 on their own machine as a local client of a remote reflow2 server named by URL: flo2's api.flo2.io, or an organization's own shared server. Their agent (Claude Code, Grok Build, any MCP client) talks to it over stdio exactly as it talks to a local reflow2, and cannot tell the difference.

IN ANTHONY'S WORDS, 2026-09-25: "a small client that gets installed locally that acts at the intermediary between flo2.io reflow2 mcp and the local claude code CLI or grok build? The agent then talks to the intermediary and knows no difference of whether it is talking to the local reflow2 mcp or the remote/centrally hosted mcp" — and, on choosing it: "my brother has discussed having their own shared reflow2 mcp at work that everybody has access to, so option c would support that, it would just be pointing it some local url_to_shared_reflow2_server.organization.org ... instead of pointing it to api.flo2.io".

WHAT "KNOWS NO DIFFERENCE" HAS TO COVER:
1. THE CREDENTIAL, AND NO ONE WAY OF GETTING IT IS HARDCODED. Anthony, 2026-09-25: "we don't hardcode option (a) as how everybody will have to access their remote mcp server". The client supports whatever the server's operator chooses:
   - NONE, for a server reached over a private network or VPN;
   - A KEY OR TOKEN THE PERSON SUPPLIES, however their organization issues it, read from an environment variable, a file or the OS keychain, and sent as a header;
   - A SIGN-IN FLOW (browser or device code) for a server that offers one.
   Whichever it is, the client keeps it out of the agent's environment where it can. Choosing among them is the server operator's policy, not reflow2's. flo2 chooses sign-in for api.flo2.io because of its own req:no-user-api-keys; an organization's shared server may hand out keys. reflow2 itself still authenticates nothing (dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id).
2. WHO A WRITE IS FOR. On a stateless server the only way to say it is per request, so the client carries `_meta["reflow2/writes_for"]` on every call it forwards (the writes_for tool, v0.71.0). A shared credential says which client, never which person.
3. THE FILES. A remote server would measure artifact files on its own disk. The client runs on the person's machine, so it measures local files and sends their checksums as asserted. Without this, the agent can tell the difference the first time it reconciles. (REVISED 2026-09-27: this point also said the client "can write the export into the local working tree". That half is WITHDRAWN by rule 3 of dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy: an export is a copy at one moment reflow2 never tracks, so nothing keeps one current. The file-measuring half stands.)

ALREADY HALF-BUILT: `--shared` is a stdio client that forwards to a `--serve-shared` HTTP daemon on loopback. This is that client, pointed at a remote address and carrying a credential.

ORDER, set by Anthony 2026-09-25: flo2's direct sign-in (option a, flo2's cap:mcp-endpoint) first, then this.

THIS IS AN ADDITION, NEVER A REPLACEMENT. Working entirely on one machine stays exactly as it is (req:reflow2-keeps-working-entirely-on-one-machine). Remote is a choice a person makes by naming a URL, and nothing about the local setup changes because it exists.

═══ 2026-09-25 — AN API KEY IN AN ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE IS A SUPPORTED WAY IN, NOT A PRECLUDED ONE ═══
Anthony: "if the reflow2 client handles this, the agent never sees the api-key. Assuming that is true ... allowing somebody to create an environment variable with an api-key is instead of using the browser sign-in I think would be acceptable. In highly technical coding jobs, environment variables are pretty common practice, so I don't we should preclude it from being used with reflow2."

WHAT THE CLIENT CAN GUARANTEE: the key never travels through MCP. It appears in no tool call, tool result, log line or error the agent reads, because the client adds it to the outbound request itself.

WHAT IT CANNOT GUARANTEE, recorded so the premise is not read as stronger than it is: a variable exported in the person's shell profile is also in the environment of every shell command the agent runs, so an agent with shell access on the same account can read it, and so can any text that talks the agent into reading it. That is true of any secret on a machine the agent can run commands on. It narrows with placement rather than disappearing: a key set only in the client's own launch entry, or read from a file or keychain entry the variable NAMES, is not in the agent's shell environment by default. The client should accept all three and its documentation should say which is least exposed. This is guidance, never a refusal.
